title: Preflight Orchestration Bridge and KPI Anchors
body:
Purpose:
To provide a compact, operational preflight guide that bridges product ops, engineering, and SRE for staged rollouts. This doc is intentionally lightweight (single-pane) to be used as the day-of checklist for traffic decisions and KPI gating.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Redwood hosted + dedicated launch tracks where we control traffic shaping. Not a replacement for full launch playbooks; this is the operational bridge for the first 14 days post-launch.
- Audience: product-ops PMs, release engineers, on-call SRE, growth/eng owners.

Summary:
We treat the first two weeks as a calibrated runway split into three phases (Smoke, Ramp, Scale). Each phase has three signal classes: Safety (SRE), Quality (product), and Economics (finance/product ops). The doc lists the anchor KPIs, owners, gating thresholds, and immediate mitigation steps.

Quick reference: phases and max daily traffic (example):
- Phase 0: Canary / Smoke — 0.1% user traffic or <= 50 TPS (whatever hits first). Duration: 1–2 days. Primary objective: verify end-to-end latency and error budgets.
- Phase 1: Controlled Ramp — 1% -> 10% over 72h. Objective: validate QA test vectors at scale, spot cost anomalies.
- Phase 2: Scale to Target — 10% -> 100% in defined steps with 24h soak between major jumps. Objective: business adoption and stress ceilings.

KPI anchors (signal definitions and thresholds):
1) Safety signals (owned by SRE):
   - p95 inference latency (hosted API): anchor threshold <= 500ms. Alert if sustained > 650ms for 10m.
   - 5xx error rate (service-level): anchor <= 0.5%. Escalate at >1.5% for 5m.
   - Queue depth / backpressure count: anchor <= 20 concurrent queued requests per node.

2) Quality signals (owned by product & QA):
   - Prompt accuracy regression (eval harness): delta <= 1.5% from baseline on core prompt set. Fail rollout if >3.0% for two consecutive evaluation runs.
   - New user-facing hallucination incidents: <= 2/day in earliest Ramp.
   - Function-calling / structured output regression: schema failures <= 0.2% of calls.

3) Economics signals (owned by product-ops & finance):
   - Cost per 1k tokens (projected): within +15% of estimate.
   - Token usage growth rate vs forecast: +/- 20% acceptable. If > +50%, throttle expansion.

Runway matrix (owner, slack, decision window):
- Product-Ops (Owner: Riley Chen) — Slack: can hold ramp for 24h to investigate quality signals. Decision window: 6h for minor regressions, 24h for major regressions.
- Eng Release Lead (Owner: Jonah Rivera) — Slack: can rollback or toggle model variant; decision window: 15m for severe safety alerts.
- SRE On-call (Owner: Maya Patel) — Slack: can scale capacity and adjust autoscale knobs; decision window: 10m for latency/error spikes.

Day-of checklist (to be completed before any major jump):
- [ ] Confirm latest canary telemetry (APM) is green (no persistent errors).
- [ ] Confirm eval harness run is within quality delta for top 200 prompts.
- [ ] Confirm cost projection vs 24h rolling cost is within expected band.
- [ ] Stakeholder sync (5–10 min) between product-ops, SRE, and release lead.
- [ ] Snapshot config: record model variant, quantization profile, autoscale policy, and traffic capping values.
- [ ] Confirm rollback plan (route to previous model, reduce traffic to 0.5%).

Contingency plays (short, actionable):
- Latency spike (>650ms p95 for 10m):
  1) Apply fast-fallback: route new requests to lower-latency model variant (observable tag: model=v1i-fast).
  2) Temporarily reduce burst window and lower batch size in serving runtime.
  3) If persists, cut traffic to prior stable percentage and page eng on-call.

- Error surge (5xx > 1.5% for 5m):
  1) Throttle non-critical routes (campaigns, background tasks).
  2) Route critical flows to Dedicated GPU pool if available.
  3) Rollback recent config delta (kernel/quantization changes).

- Quality regression (eval delta > 3%):
  1) Pause ramp; trigger immediate canary replay of failing prompts to inspect outputs.
  2) Swap model to previous version pinned in config.
  3) Notify legal/comms if regression impacts safety-sensitive verticals.

Signal collection notes (observability hooks):
- Ensure eval harness runs hourly for first 48h, then 6h cadence until day 14.
- Hook: slack-channel #launch-signals for top alerts; automated summary every 30m during ramp windows.
- Trace IDs for problematic requests should be surfaced to a centralized extraction table (sheet) with owner + timestamp.

Communication template (15–30 lines for status updates):
- Subject: [LAUNCH PRELIGHT] <product-name> — Phase <n> — <green/yellow/red>
- TL;DR: current traffic %, key signal deltas, immediate action (if any).
- Details: latency p95, 5xx rate, eval delta, cost delta, next decision time.
- Action owners: list names and contactable runbooks.

Decision rubric (simple, for rapid binary choices):
- Green: all anchors within thresholds -> proceed with scheduled ramp step.
- Yellow: one non-critical anchor breached (mild) -> hold for investigation 1–6h, no further ramp.
- Red: any Safety anchor breached or Quality anchor > 3% -> rollback or reduce traffic and open incident.

Post-mortem and metric capture (first 14 days):
- Owners must populate the Launch Lightboard sheet within 24h of any triggered mitigation. Required fields: timestamp, trigger, p95, 5xx%, cost delta, mitigation action, owner notes.
- 72h checkpoint: product ops to produce a short blameless summary of emergent patterns and one tactical change.

Open questions / decisions to make before next major launch:
- Should we raise p95 latency anchor for Dedicated customers to reflect SLA commitments? (action: product-ops + SRE to propose values)
- Is the 14-day observation window sufficient for model-behavior regressions tied to prompt drift? (action: research team to recommend extended monitoring hooks)

Appendix: Example command snippets (for release engineers)
- Snapshot config: curl -X GET https://internal-api/configs/current?env=prod | jq . > launch-snapshot.json
- Toggle traffic (example): POST /internal/traffic-control { "route": "/v1/generate", "percent": 0.01 } (auth via release service token)

Notes and context: lightweight doc intentionally mixes prose and operational bullets so it can be copied into a shared-slack thread or pinned in a release incident. This is not exhaustive; use this as the canonical day-of decision bridge and link to longer runbooks for deep diagnostics.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-15: initial draft (Riley Chen)
- 2024-12-05: added economics anchors and ramp cadence details (Priya Nair)
- 2025-01-10: clarified contingency plays and integrated SRE feedback (Maya Patel)
